title: Honest status: writing what is true
summary: Drake writes status in a fixed shape: the thing and its level, what the level rests on, and what is not done. Words like done, fully and production-ready carry no evidence, and QUALIFIED or PASS need a receipt on the same line. He never relabels old receipts or edits history; corrections go beside the old record. I can rewrite a status with you, and run overclaim.om, an Omega word check, on the before and after text.
goal: Write a status line that says what was shown and what was not, and catch common overclaim words mechanically.
key_steps: Name the thing and its narrowest level
Say what the level rests on: a number with its source, or a receipt
Say what is not done, with NOT_RUN where it applies
Remove evidence-free words like done, fully, production-ready
Never relabel an old status or receipt; add a new one or a correction beside it
Run the overclaim check before publishing

example.code:
note overclaim: read status text on stdin and flag words that claim more than evidence can carry
note list a is always flagged; list b (ladder and verdict words) is flagged unless the same line also
note carries a receipt reference or a negation; a word is letters, digits, _ - and %
note exit 0 no flags, 1 flags found, 4 REFUSED (input too big)
text wa "production-ready blazing guaranteed fully done Done works bulletproof 100% "
text wb "QUALIFIED DEPLOYED VERIFIED PASS verified qualified deployed "
text wx "receipt not NOT NOT_RUN Nothing "
text tline "line "
text ta ": always an overclaim: "
text tb ": ladder word with no receipt or negation on the line: "
text tflags "flags "
text vclean "verdict CLEAN\n"
text vover "verdict OVERCLAIM\n"
text nl "\n"
note ln: 0 line number, 1 flags
global ln ulong 2
fn isw c uchar to bool
if and ge c 97 le c 122
ret true
end
if and ge c 65 le c 90
ret true
end
if and ge c 48 le c 57
ret true
end
ret or or eq c 95 eq c 45 eq c 37
end
fn wend a ulong b ulong to ulong
e = a
while lt e b bound 524289
if not isw get inb e
ret e
end
e = add e 1
end
ret e
end
fn excused a ulong b ulong to bool
note does the line a .. b-1 carry a word from wx
i = a
while lt i b bound 524289
e = wend i b
if lt i e
if ge lookup wx i e 0
ret true
end
i = e
else
i = add i 1
end
end
ret false
end
fn flag t view uchar * a ulong e ulong to void
ot tline
on get ln 0
ot t
oi a e
ot nl
put ln 1 add get ln 1 1
end
fn oneline a ulong b ulong to void
put ln 0 add get ln 0 1
x = excused a b
i = a
while lt i b bound 524289
e = wend i b
if lt i e
if ge lookup wa i e 0
flag ta i e
end
if not x
if ge lookup wb i e 0
flag tb i e
end
end
i = e
else
i = add i 1
end
end
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 4
end
if eq get st 2 1
ret 4
end
n = ulong r
a = ulong 0
for i ulong n
if eq get inb i 10
oneline a i
a = add i 1
end
end
if lt a n
oneline a n
end
ot tflags
on get ln 1
ot nl
v = int 0
if gt get ln 1 0
v = 1
ot vover
else
ot vclean
end
f = flush
ret v
end

omc sha256 befb8199db8c4bca188a494dfaac2a6f0ee5c36fcea11188c75666c55fce8a1d
compile lib.om+overclaim.om rc=0

line 1: always an overclaim: fully

line 2: ladder word with no receipt or negation on the line: QUALIFIED
line 3: ladder word with no receipt or negation on the line: verified
line 3: ladder word with no receipt or negation on the line: PASS
line 3: always an overclaim: blazing
flags 7

run rc=1

every verdict as expected: yes

common_mistake: Deleting the flagged word and keeping the claim ('the installer is ready'). Rewrite to the shape instead. And never edit last week's status upward because a later run went well; write a new one.
